newsitem.title: JAPAN: DVD inventors agree on DVD-RAM, DVD-R formats.
newsitem.headline: DVD inventors agree on DVD-RAM, DVD-R formats.

text.p: Toshiba Corp said on Monday that it and the nine other joint inventors of digital video discs (DVDs) had agreed on a standard format for flexible-use DVDs.

The agreed specifications are for rewritable DVD-RAMs, on which data can be entered and rewritten over and over again, and another version, DVD-Rs, which can be rewritten once. The discs offer more flexibility than non-rewritable DVD-ROMs, in which the stored data is fixed.
The agreed standards for DVD-RAMs and DVD-Rs will help expand the potential of DVDs as a medium with large storage capacity, Toshiba said in a statement.
The 10 companies will issue format books detailing the specifications in the middle of April, it said.
"They will be available to all interested parties and will be further promoted in a series of conferences in Japan, the United States and Europe from late April onwards," Toshiba said.

The nine other firms are Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd, Pioneer Electronic Corp, Victor Co of Japan, Mitsubishi Electric Co, Hitachi Ltd, Sony Corp, Philips Electronics NV, Thomson SA and Time Warner Inc.
They launched DVD players and non-rewritable DVD-ROM discs late last year but had yet to agree on the format for the more flexible versions.

Under the agreed standard, DVD-RAMs adopt a recording method called the wobble land groove recording method, which records signals on both the lands -- the area between grooves -- and the grooves formed on the disc, Toshiba said.
The capacity of a single-sided DVD-RAM disc is 2.6 gigabytes and a doubled-sided disc has twice that capacity, it said.
Modulation and error correction codes are the same as for DVD-video and DVD-ROM, assuring compatibility with other DVD formats, Toshiba said.
A DVD-R disc has a single-side storage capacity of 3.95 gigabytes and double that capacity for a two-sided disc, Toshiba said.
